title: Per-head attention telemetry and staged rollback policy for v3 integrations
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: instrument the serving runtime to emit per-layer and per-head latency, workspace usage, and kernel decision telemetry, and build a staged rollback policy that can disable FlashAttention v3 variants at layer/head granularity when regressions are detected. Motivation: recent v3 rollouts show rare but high-impact p95 latency spikes and token regressions that appear correlated with a small subset of attention heads and specific shapes. Current probes are coarse (per-request or per-layer only) and miss the head-level signal needed to safely gate rollouts without global rollbacks.

Scope and deliverables:
- Runtime instrumentation: add lightweight per-head timing counters and memory delta metrics around the attention kernel hot path. Metrics must be aggregate-friendly (prometheus-friendly names) and attach to request traces for sampled requests.
- Kernel decision tagging: record the chosen kernel variant (fa2/fa3/legacy/quant-shim) and key shape fingerprint alongside telemetry so we can correlate choices with observed regressions.
- Telemetry export: wire new metrics to the existing telemetry pipeline and add a dashboard with head-level heatmaps, p50/p95/p99 latency per head, and count of kernel switches per rolling minute.
- Canary and synthetic harness: expand the runtime canary to exercise skewed head activity patterns (long context + narrow per-head load) and measure sensitivity. Add a synthetic generator that can reproduce observed spike profiles.
- Staged rollback policy: implement a policy engine that can mark kernel variants as disabled for specific model/layer/head tuples when metric thresholds are exceeded. Policy should support: threshold-based autosussension, manual overrides, and automated recovery after a cooldown window.
- Safety and observability: ensure every automated suspension emits an audit event (model, layer, head, triggering metric, timestamp, and initiating rule) and create a quick remediation runbook for on-call.

Acceptance criteria:
- Per-head latency and memory metrics recorded with <=7% overhead on p99 throughput in microbench harness.
- Dashboard shows heatmap and allows drilldown to sample traces with kernel tags.
- Canary reproduces at least one historical incident profile in synthetic mode.
- Staged rollback can disable a v3 kernel for a single layer/head and restore it automatically after cooldown; verified via end-to-end test.
- No customer-facing error increase when running the staging policy in shadow mode for 48 hours.

Risk and trade-offs:
- Over-instrumentation could add latency or noise; we will start with sampled traces and aggregate counters, not per-token timers.
- Per-head rollback increases decision complexity; we will restrict initial rollout to non-critical models and a small traffic bucket.
- Kernel tagging will enlarge telemetry cardinality; we'll apply shape fingerprinting and cardinality caps to avoid ingestion storms.

Implementation plan and milestones:
1) 2026-02-24 to 2026-03-03: prototype per-head counters in a forked runtime branch; run microbench to measure overhead.
2) 2026-03-04 to 2026-03-11: add kernel decision tagging and shape fingerprinting; integrate with trace sampler.
3) 2026-03-12 to 2026-03-18: telemetry export and dashboard mockups; synthetic harness for skewed head loads.
4) 2026-03-19 to 2026-03-25: staged rollback policy implementation and unit/integration tests; run shadow policy.
5) 2026-03-26 to 2026-03-28: canary rollout to a small slice of traffic, monitor, iterate, and prepare release notes.

Notes for reviewers:
- Benchmarks are included in the runtime PR; please focus on overhead numbers and cardinality controls in the telemetry integration.
- The rollback engine is intentionally conservative: it will only activate in canary traffic initially.

Longer-term ideas (out of scope for this ticket):
- Auto-synthesis of head load patterns from production traces to continuously expand the canary corpus.
- Machine-learned head-level regressors that predict when a head is likely to misbehave under v3 kernels and preemptively route to a fallback.
